modes.boundary: A user-supplied detail echoed back as a verified order field is this mode only when the detail reaches a refund, a cancellation or a ticket - that is, when it is written into a record or put in front of a human. modes.name: invented_date_reasoning
modes.definition: Fail when the agent states or relies on how much time has passed without a dated source for today, and the claim is false or drives a decision. Two shapes count: (a) asserting a window has passed, is overdue or is outside the limit; (b) asserting that the user's stated timing conflicts with the record when the two in fact agree. Both rest on the same missing input — the agent has no authoritative current date.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent relies on refund_eligible without making a date claim (support-0034); an unsourced but correct and inconsequential date remark (support-0066) is a boundary case to decide. Shape (b) is the inverse of shape (a) and is easy to miss: in support-0036 the user said 'like 8 days ago', the record agreed, and the agent called it a discrepancy and escalated on it. The original support-0114 trace is the close negative for shape (b): same setup, and the agent made no date claim at all. Differs from refusal_mishandled: a correct refusal can still invent a date, and vice versa.
modes.spec_ref: RESP-9 (added 2026-09-20; clarifies RESP-3 for elapsed-time claims), RESP-3
modes.product_change: Give the agent today's date in the session context; rule: no elapsed-time claims without a dated source. Evidence: in support-0198 the agent substituted the real-world date ('Current date 2026-09-14'), so the fix must supply the world date explicitly.

modes.name: refusal_mishandled
modes.definition: Fail when a rule or a tool result forbids what the user asked for — the refund is not eligible, the order has already shipped, or the caller has no permission for it — and the reply does not refuse clearly, naming the governing rule and the next step. Counted as failing: presenting refund_eligible: false as a failed 'automatic' check a human may override; citing the wrong return window (support-0091); opening a ticket or offering an 'exception' that no policy provides; and escalating after permission_denied without first asking the user to confirm the order number. Pass when the agent refuses and cites the rule that governs the refusal, or refuses after permission_denied and asks the user to re-check the number.
modes.boundary: Not this mode when the agent refuses and explains the governing rule with a citation (support-0034), or refuses after permission_denied and asks to double-check the number (support-0236, support-0238). A ticket is fine when an ESC rule lists the case, the user reports something to investigate (support-0024, misrouting) or confirms after being asked (support-0046). An accurate refusal that omits the reason, especially when the user asked for brevity, is a boundary case (support-0025). Differs from invented_date_reasoning: a correct refusal can still invent a date, and vice versa. Differs from out_of_scope_not_declined: that is about requests outside Cartwheel support.
modes.evaluator: code check + LLM judge. Code detects the trigger (refund_eligible false, or a tool returning not_eligible or permission_denied) and any escalate_to_human call that follows it; the judge decides whether the reply refuses clearly and names the governing rule.
modes.product_change: Refusal rule: when a tool or record says no, say so, give the governing rule (store or platform window, shipped status, no access) and the next step; open a ticket only when an ESC rule lists the case; after permission_denied, ask the user to confirm the order number first.

modes.name: inconsistent_record_not_flagged
modes.definition: Fail when the agent asserts a fact from, or acts on, an order record that contradicts itself or another record, without stating the contradiction. The contradiction may be visible inside a single tool result (a ship date after the delivery date; a 'delivered' status with no delivery date) or it may require a second lookup that the request itself turns on (an order whose product belongs to a different store than the order). Pass when the agent states the contradiction, declines to assert a timeline, a deadline or a seller from it, and escalates.
modes.boundary: The hinge is whether the reply states the contradiction, not whether the agent could refuse anyway. A missing field is in scope when the record still claims otherwise (support-0208: status 'delivered' with no delivery date, never mentioned) and out of scope when the agent names the gap and does not compute from it (support-0028, support-0209, support-0210, support-0211). A second lookup is expected only when the request depends on the relationship in question — in support-0221 the user asked which store handles the order, so the product's store had to be checked; a routine status lookup does not oblige the agent to audit every field. Differs from user_claim_not_reconciled: there a user's claim conflicts with the record; here the record is inconsistent on its own, whether or not the user says so. Resolved from batch 3: support-0045 (a store mismatch the user doubted) is a positive for both this mode and user_claim_not_reconciled. The record is inconsistent on its own and the request turned on the store, so this mode applies; the user's doubt being dismissed is what the other mode names. A trace may carry more than one mode.
modes.evaluator: code check + LLM judge. Code detects the contradictory record (dates out of order, status conflicting with the dates, order store not equal to the product's store); the judge decides whether the reply states it and refrains from asserting from it.
modes.product_change: Rule: before using an order record, check that its dates are in order and its store matches the product; if not, state the inconsistency, do not assert a timeline, and escalate.

Differs from user_claim_not_reconciled: there a user's claim conflicts with the record; here the record is inconsistent by itself. support-0045 (store mismatch the user doubted) stays in user_claim_not_reconciled; revisit in Part D.
boundary.to: The hinge is whether the reply states the contradiction, not whether the agent could refuse anyway. A missing field is in scope when the record still claims otherwise (support-0208: status 'delivered' with no delivery date, never mentioned) and out of scope when the agent names the gap and does not compute from it (support-0028, support-0209, support-0210, support-0211). A second lookup is expected only when the request depends on the relationship in question — in support-0221 the user asked which store handles the order, so the product's store had to be checked; a routine status lookup does not oblige the agent to audit every field. Differs from user_claim_not_reconciled: there a user's claim conflicts with the record; here the record is inconsistent on its own, whether or not the user says so. Open item carried from batch 3: support-0045 (a store mismatch the user doubted) is still placed in user_claim_not_reconciled and may belong in both.

evaluator.to: code check + LLM judge. Code detects the contradictory record (dates out of order, status conflicting with the dates, order store not equal to the product's store); the judge decides whether the reply states it and refrains from asserting from it.

Marked final at the end of Part D. Checked against the handout's per-mode requirements: snake_case name, a binary definition another reviewer can apply, at least three confirmed positives, at least three close negatives, the originating human annotations, a boundary against the nearest mode, a likely evaluator type, and a requirement source in SPEC.md. The taxonomy was then compared with the AgentErrorTaxonomy (arXiv 2509.25370); that comparison produced one rename and two rejected additions, and no new mode.

modes.name: product_record_defect_not_flagged
modes.definition: Considered and rejected. Would have read: the agent presents a defective catalog record - a negative price, an empty title, or one of several identically titled listings - as a valid product fact, without saying the record is wrong or ambiguous.
modes.boundary: Would have differed from inconsistent_record_not_flagged in the object: that mode is about order records that contradict themselves or another record, this one about product records holding invalid or missing values. By the merge/split test they are separate: correcting them needs catalog validation, not record reconciliation.
modes.spec_ref: would have needed a new requirement; none written
modes.evaluator: code check (price <= 0, empty title, duplicate title within a store) + LLM judge
modes.product_change: Validate catalog values before quoting them; state the defect instead of the value.

revisions.note: Rejected group, Part D. A repeat search against the seed catalog found 16 traces surfacing the three product-level data-quality cases (dq-product-duplicate-title on products 1 and 2, dq-product-missing-title on product 3, dq-product-invalid-price on product 4). Rejected on the evidence: only 4 of the 16 fall inside the reviewed sample, the reviewer had already read all four and recorded no failure, and three of them serve as close negatives for other modes today (support-0030, support-0047, support-0049, support-0227). The agent handles these records well in almost every trace - it names the blank title, calls the negative price a listing error, and lists the duplicate titles with their identifiers. One trace looks like a genuine miss, support-0223, which answers 'what's the price?' with 'The Rustic Pitcher is listed at -$5.00' against an expected outcome of do_not_present_negative_price_as_valid_offer, and even there the agent corrects itself in turn 2 when asked. One unreviewed trace does not support a mode: the handout allows an addition only when the reviewer's own traces and annotations back it. Recorded here so the considered alternative stays inspectable, and as the candidate to revisit if Homework 5 needs an eighth mode.
